subject: iceCreamCart
pitch: A cheerful seaside ice cream cart. A mint and cream body with a scalloped striped canopy in pink and white, two big spoked wheels, a push handle, a chrome lid over the freezer, a hand-painted sign shaped like a cone, and a row of giant fake ice cream cones in pastel flavours along the top.
reasoning:
I don't have the full API surface, so I need to stick carefully to only the documented SDK functions I'm confident about—things like createBuilder and the various b. methods for joints, chains, parts, and surface decoration—rather than guessing at unlisted ones.

Now I'm sketching the cart's actual geometry: a mint-colored boxy body around 1.1m wide, 0.9m tall, 1.8m deep, with a chrome half-cylinder freezer lid on top, all positioned relative to a root joint so the proportions read clearly as an ice cream cart standing on the ground.

Setting up spoked wheel rigs now: torus tires rotated into the correct plane, hub cylinders along the axle, and thin box spokes arranged radially around each wheel joint.

Checking how wheels sit against the body to make sure proportions look right, then moving on to designing the canopy with alternating pink and white scalloped stripe panels supported by corner posts.

Still placing scallops and support posts...

Actually boxes are safer than rods since I'd need rotation math for angled struts — I'll build the handlebar and uprights with simple box geometries instead, positioning each at the right coordinates.

For the sign, I'm wary of using unfamiliar texture/paint APIs, so I'll keep it as a plain-colored cone (tip pointing down like an ice cream cone) mounted on a post near the front of the body, avoiding risky calls like stripes or svg textures I'm not confident about.

I'm now working out the sign's placement: a tip-down cone with a scoop sphere resting on top mimics an ice cream cone shape, but I need to check its position doesn't collide with the canopy valance, so I may need to shift it to the side instead of dead-center front.

Still working out the sign post geometry...

Now I'm thinking about adding a row of decorative ice cream cones along the top of the canopy roof — upright cones with tip pointing down, topped with pastel colored scoop spheres (mint, pink, lemon, lavender) spaced across the roof edge.

Actually simplifying to 4 cones spaced along z at -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, radius 0.18, scoop 0.24, tips embedded right at the canopy roof height of 2.1.

Overall height lands around 3.04 which feels reasonable for a cart with oversized cones on top. I'm now settling on a palette: pastel mint, strawberry, lemon, lavender for flavor colors, tan waffle for the cones, mint body with cream trim panels, pink and white canopy, and a dark recessed serving window.

Positioning the window, counter shelf, cone sign, and chrome freezer lid on the body, checking that the sign post clears the counter and the canopy posts sit properly behind without collision. I'm verifying ground clearance works out with the body bottom and wheel placement, keeping everything structurally consistent.

Now I'm adding a dark chassis box underneath and working out wheel placement with axles outside the chassis half-width, using spoke geometry attached via joints to the axle positions, and checking the wheel z-position stays within the cart's length.

I'm orienting the torus tire in the YZ plane and the cylindrical hub along X, then placing six box-shaped spokes rotated around X at 30-degree intervals so they span the hub-to-tire radius correctly. I'm also considering a cream decorative side panel for the body as a stylistic touch.

For the rig, I'm thinking through how joints and parent relationships work in this system — deciding to keep things simple with just a single root joint for the cart and treating wheels/axles as plain parts rather than wiring up a full joint hierarchy, since props don't strictly need bones. I still need to add the meta export with name and description, and set up materials using hex color strings.

For visual detail, I'm planning to add sprinkles on top of the ice cream scoops using small boxes scattered via a seeded random function, calculating their positions along the upper hemisphere of each scoop using spherical coordinates so they look naturally distributed rather than clustered.

Building the cart body...

Working out the roof stripe positions and alternating colors, then sizing the canopy posts to span from the body top down to the roof underside.

I realize the back posts align fine but the front posts at z 1.25 would float beyond the body edge since the body only extends to z 0.9, so I'm repositioning them to z 0.85 and -0.85 to sit flush on the body while letting the canopy overhang slightly in front.

Working out the roof panel dimensions, I set the canopy spanning z -0.9 to 1.3 and divide it into six stripes about 0.37 wide, computing their center positions so they tile evenly across that length with a slight overhang at the front edge.

For the scalloped valance along the front edge, I'm placing eight small spheres evenly spaced across the width in alternating pink and white to create a decorative trim just below the roofline.

Now I'm figuring out the valance along the sides too, spacing spheres roughly every 0.2 units in z, accepting some overlap with the support posts for a stylized look, then working out the cone finials on top — sizing and rotating cones so their tips align with the roof's peak and spacing four of them evenly across the ridge.

I'm adding a torus ring at each cone's base plus a scoop-shaped sphere sitting partly sunken into the cone to look like ice cream, then scattering small cube "sprinkles" in a spiral pattern across each scoop's surface using spherical coordinates to position them realistically.

For color variety I'm defining four pastel flavor colors—mint, strawberry, lemon, lavender—cycling through them for each of the four cones. I'm also working out the sign's cone geometry and the arm connecting it, positioning the scoop and attachment points so the proportions look right.

Now I'm designing the push handle for the cart, working out the bar and upright struts that attach it to the body, calculating positions and dimensions so it looks structurally plausible.

Checking the sink depth confirms the tire dips only about 1.3% into the floor, well within tolerance, so I'm fine there. Now I'm positioning the wheels at ±0.66 on the x-axis and setting up the tire torus geometry, rotated to sit correctly on the axle, before moving on to the rim and hub pieces.

Writing wheel geometry code...

For color, I'm thinking a pink-and-dark scheme works nicely: dark tire ("#2e2e38") paired with pink spokes and hubs ("#ff6fa5"), placed at each wheel center and looped across both sides of the cart to keep it symmetric.

Now I'm double-checking the builder's part signature and confirming a short helper function for placing geometry with color and position, keeping imports minimal to just the builder and THREE before finalizing the scoop shape and writing the full module.
